chains.title: T strengthens FOXA1-dependent TOX3 enhancer activity
chains.element: The variant lies in a candidate cis-regulatory element that enhances TOX3 expression.
chains.cell_type: Luminal breast cancer cells, including MCF7.

links.claim: FOXA1 is the leading candidate based on the reported biology of this breast-cancer locus; this hypothesis is that alt T binds FOXA1 more strongly. No QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here to establish the allelic direction.
The variant-containing sequence acts as a FOXA1-responsive enhancer.
The effect occurs in luminal breast cells where FOXA1 is relevant, such as MCF7.
Increased TOX3 expression contributes to increased breast-cancer susceptibility.

predictions: The T allele will show greater FOXA1 occupancy than C at the endogenous site.
The T-containing element will drive more enhancer activity and higher TOX3 expression than the C-containing element in a relevant breast-cell context.
falsified_if: Allele-resolved occupancy shows no T-biased FOXA1 binding, or shows stronger binding to C.
The T allele does not increase enhancer output or TOX3 expression in an appropriate breast-cell context.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The variant will show no reproducible allele-dependent TF occupancy or regulatory output in an appropriate breast-cell context.
Any association may reflect linkage to another causal variant or another non-TF-mediated explanation.
falsified_if: Endogenous allele replacement produces a reproducible TF-dependent change in regulatory output and a downstream gene-expression effect.

chains.title: T strengthens FOXA1 binding but reduces TOX3 enhancer output
chains.element: The variant-containing sequence is a FOXA1-responsive regulatory element whose output is repressive in this context.
chains.cell_type: Luminal breast cancer cells, including MCF7.

links.claim: FOXA1 is the candidate TF; this alternative also hypothesizes stronger binding to alt T, but no QBiC-SELEX result is supplied to establish that direction.
The variant-containing element recruits FOXA1 in a context where FOXA1 binding reduces its enhancer output.
Reduced element output lowers TOX3 expression.
The regulatory effect occurs in luminal breast cells, including MCF7.
Reduced TOX3 expression increases breast-cancer susceptibility.

predictions: The T allele will show greater FOXA1 occupancy than C.
Despite greater occupancy, the T-containing element will produce less reporter activity and lower TOX3 expression than the C-containing element.
falsified_if: The T allele does not show greater FOXA1 occupancy.
The T-containing element increases rather than reduces regulatory output and TOX3 expression.

chains.title: A different luminal TF mediates the allele effect on TOX3
chains.element: The variant-containing sequence is a GATA3-responsive enhancer of TOX3.

links.claim: GATA3 is an alternative luminal TF candidate; this hypothesis is that ref C binds it more strongly. No QBiC-SELEX result or allele-specific occupancy evidence is supplied for GATA3.
The variant-containing sequence acts as a GATA3-responsive enhancer.
GATA3-dependent activity of the element increases TOX3 expression.
The effect occurs in GATA3-expressing luminal breast cells.
The resulting change in TOX3 expression contributes to breast-cancer susceptibility.

predictions: The C allele will show greater GATA3 occupancy than T.
Changing GATA3 abundance or activity will alter the allele-dependent effect on TOX3.
falsified_if: GATA3 does not occupy the variant-containing element in relevant cells.
The allelic effect persists unchanged when GATA3 activity is reduced.

matrix.test: Paired C-versus-T enhancer reporter assay in MCF7 cells, with TOX3 enhancer output measured.

outcomes.outcome: T gives higher reporter activity than C.
T gives lower reporter activity than C.
C is predicted to give higher activity; the effect should depend on GATA3.
No reproducible difference between C and T.

matrix.test: Allele-resolved FOXA1 occupancy at the endogenous variant in heterozygous MCF7 cells.

outcomes.outcome: FOXA1 occupancy need not be allele-biased.
No variant-linked allele bias in occupancy.

matrix.test: Measure allele-specific TOX3 expression after endogenous C-to-T or T-to-C editing in a relevant breast-cell model.

outcomes.outcome: The expression effect depends on GATA3 and favors the C allele.
Editing the variant alone produces no reproducible TOX3 expression change.

next_experiment: Run the low-cost paired C-versus-T enhancer reporter assay in MCF7 cells. It directly distinguishes the top two hypotheses by testing whether the T allele raises or lowers regulatory output; a positive result would still need endogenous validation.
